title: Normalization and simultaneous models for finite coefficient-system operations
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi$, and schemes $W$ on which $\ell$ is invertible [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension, def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. On each small pro-etale site set $B_{W,n}=(\mathcal O_E/\varpi^n)_W$ for $n\ge1$ and $R_W=\lim_n B_{W,n}$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Work in the ordinary unbounded derived category $\mathscr D_W=D(\mathscr S(B_{W,\bullet}))$ of whole semilinear systems, with its tensor and geometric inverse image [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections]. A normalized system has invertible transition adjoints $\alpha^A_{m,n}:q_W^*A_m\to A_n$, where $q_W^*=-\otimes^L_{B_{W,m}}B_{W,n}$, for all $m\ge n\ge1$, with the identity and quotient cocycles [def-coef-normalized-dvr-tower]. For systems $A,N$ on $W$ and $C$ on $Y$, write $T_W(A,N)_n=A_n\otimes^L_{B_{W,n}}N_n$, $F_f(C)_n=Lf_n^*C_n$ for $f:X\to Y$, and $U_W=(B_{W,n}[0])_n$, with the induced whole-system transitions.

These whole-system operations preserve normalization, with precisely the following adjoint transition maps:
$$q_W^*T_W(A,N)_m\xrightarrow{\sim}q_W^*A_m\otimes^L_{B_{W,n}}q_W^*N_m\xrightarrow{\alpha^A_{m,n}\otimes\alpha^N_{m,n}}T_W(A,N)_n,$$
$$q_X^*Lf_m^*C_m\xrightarrow{\kappa^{-1}}Lf_n^*q_Y^*C_m\xrightarrow{Lf_n^*(\alpha^C_{m,n})}Lf_n^*C_n.$$
The first arrow in the first display is monoidal scalar extension. The coefficient square defining $\kappa$ commutes by the constant-section ring maps; $\kappa$ is the scalar-association map from $Lf_n^*q_Y^*$ to $q_X^*Lf_m^*$, whose inverse inserts $1$ in the intermediate scalar factor [lem-pur-cochain-pullback-tensor-coherence]. The actual input transition factors as $C_m\to\operatorname{Res}q_Y^*C_m\xrightarrow{\operatorname{Res}\alpha^C_{m,n}}\operatorname{Res}C_n$; the displayed adjoints specify the actual output transitions, not a replacement by canonical scalar-extension units. On flat representatives the tensor adjoint sends $(a\otimes x)\otimes b$ to $\tau_A(a)\otimes b\tau_N(x)$. For $r\ge m\ge n$ both composite output adjoints agree with the direct one: the tensor formula uses the two input cocycles and $q_{r,n}=q_{m,n}q_{r,m}$, and both pullback scalar-association composites multiply the same three scalar factors and then use the input cocycle. The unit adjoint is $B_{W,m}\otimes^L_{B_{W,m}}B_{W,n}\cong B_{W,n}$.

All these comparisons and cocycles are constructed on whole systems before evaluation. Flat-term K-flat representatives [def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules] may be chosen on the ringed sites; every finite iterated tensor or pullback, including coefficient-quotient pullback, is computed on such representatives by ordinary direct-sum total tensor and termwise inverse image. The resulting representatives remain flat-term K-flat, even for complexes unbounded in both directions; the simultaneous system models retain their transitions and coherence. No flatness of a quotient ring map is assumed.

proof.text: Use the supplied Data tensor-reduction formula. On normalized inputs its two reduction maps and the monoidal scalar comparison are invertible, so cancellation of tensor evaluation proves tensor normalization. The chain-map formula is the existing system cochain tensor reduction equation. Its section formula is the ordinary tensor transition followed by the scalar adjunction; linearity and tensor balancing give tau(x) tensor b tau(y). The supplied reduction cocycle and the ordinary input transpose supply the remaining tensor laws.

Resolve once on the sequence site by the flat-term K-flat resolution theorem. The supplied tensorEvaluationModel.kflat gives evaluated K-flatness; evaluation_preserves_flat gives evaluated termwise flatness. The direct-sum total tensor theorem gives whole and level tensor closure. Scalar change-of-rings preserves flat-term K-flat complexes, and its recorded computes isomorphism computes the quotient vertex. These are exactly the simultaneous model clauses.

The regular module is flat since tensoring with it is naturally the identity, and its degree-zero single complex is K-flat by the bounded flat-complex criterion. The evaluated regular module is identified by an explicit identity-on-section-carriers linear equivalence. For every target N, precomposition by the ordinary unit reduction is the equivalence obtained from unitHomEquiv at the two coefficient rings and the scalar adjunction. Hence that reduction is an isomorphism. Degreewise this makes the cochain unit reduction an isomorphism; the K-flat counit formula then proves normalization of the derived unit. The scalar transpose and transition of the regular sequence module give q(s)b, including zero degrees and zero rings.

Choose the geometric realization with the literal target coefficient tower using the separate canonical coefficient-system construction. The derived pulled transition formula immediately preserves normalization, since its input reduction, coefficient comparison and evaluation isomorphisms are invertible. The output reduction cocycle is the target Data reduction_cocycle. The scalar-association cocycle is proved separately by ordinary restriction-square composition, localization and the specified adjunction transposes.

For the ordinary scalar comparison, form the mate of the ordinary restrictionPullback square under the scalar adjunctions. Its further level-adjunction mate has identity underlying map under the specified direct-image identifications: expand the Hom equivalence using the level unit, use naturality, the normalized underlying-unit equation and the counit triangle. It is therefore invertible, since underlying sheaves reflect isomorphisms. The iterated-mate/conjugate-equivalence identity makes the desired scalar mate invertible as well. Its inverse defines kappa; unit_mateEquiv_symm gives exactly the required transpose. Hom-equivalence naturality and ordinaryPullTransition prove the transition equation, retaining the actual input transition.

The supplied whole and level tensor-model fields preserve K-flatness under geometric pullback. Algebraic inverse image preserves flat module sheaves at each level. Flatness of a system follows from flatness at every level: at (n,U) use the local finite-relation criterion in level n, lift its covering sieve to the sequence site, and restrict its factorization witnesses along the horizontal (m,V) to (n,V) arrow. Semilinearity and functoriality preserve both finite matrix equations, including empty families and empty covers. Thus ordinaryPullEvaluation transfers level flatness to the pulled system. Package these results with the source and target tensor, unit and model laws into the unchanged conjunction HasOperationSystemModels.
